item.title: Police say the 24-year-old who fatally shot 6 people in a Krakow square has died in the hospital
item.description:
Police say the 24-year-old who fatally shot 6 people in a Krakow square has died in the hospital
Police said the 24-year-old who opened fire in a city square in Poland, killing six people and wounding 15 on Saturday, died in the hospital Monday morningByThe Associated PressNovember 9, 2026, 1:33 AM
KRAKOW, Poland -- The 24-year-old who opened fire in a city square in Poland, killing six people and wounding 15 on Saturday, died in the hospital Monday morning, police said.
The man had been in critical condition after police shot him to end the attack and had had several operations.
The assailant drove through the square in the heart of Krakow’s Old Town on Saturday to start the attack. The square is a major tourist hub in the country’s second-largest city.

item.title: Gunman with far-right views who killed 6 people in a Polish city square dies in hospital, police say
item.description:
Gunman with far-right views who killed 6 people in a Polish city square dies in hospital, police say
Police said the 24-year-old who opened fire in a city square in Poland, killing six people and wounding 15 on Saturday, died in the hospital Monday morningByThe Associated PressNovember 9, 2026, 1:33 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
KRAKOW, Poland -- The 24-year-old with far-right views who killed six people and wounded 15 others in a shooting in a Polish city square Saturday died in the hospital Monday, police said.
The attacker, wearing military-style clothing and a bulletproof vest, drove into the Main Square in Krakow’s Old Town and opened fire. The location is a major tourist destination in Poland’s second-largest city, and several foreigners were among the dead and wounded.
Police said the man continued firing even after he was wounded by police officers. He had been in critical condition in the hospital since the attack.
Authorities also found the bodies of the assailant’s sister, mother and father at the man’s family home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers (93 miles) northeast of Krakow. They likely died from gunshot wounds.
On Sunday night, mourners laid candles and flowers alongside bullet holes in Krakow after the city’s central square turned into a site of bloodshed and grief.
“I come here so as not to get caught up in a spiral of fear and anxiety,” resident Maciej Sikorski told The Associated Press from the square. “In a situation like this, it’s all too easy to stop living — to start being afraid instead, and just vegetate. That is something I really want to avoid.”

item.title: Remembering Kristallnacht: Witness says night of terror risks being a lesson not learned
item.description:
Remembering Kristallnacht: Witness says night of terror risks being a lesson not learned
Germany is marking the 88th anniversary of the “Night of Broken Glass,” the Nazi-led attacks on Jewish communities on Nov. 9, 1938, when synagogues, homes and thousands of Jewish businesses were destroyedByKIRSTEN GRIESHABER Associated PressNovember 9, 2026, 1:06 AM
BERLIN -- George Shefi was just 6 years old on Nov. 9, 1938, when his mother kept him home for three days. When he was finally allowed to go out again, his Jewish school inside a Berlin synagogue had been burned down, the Jewish hat store opposite his home had been looted, and the windows of the stationery shop next door had been smashed.
The Jewish shop owner “was trying to clean this thing up, and there were, I don’t know, a lot of people, 30, 40, 50, or something, jeering and yelling and saying nasty things,” Shefi recalled during a recent visit to his childhood home in Berlin's Schoeneberg district.
Shefi, now 94 and a resident of Jerusalem, was describing Kristallnacht — the “Night of Broken Glass” — when Nazis, among them many ordinary Germans, terrorized Jews throughout Germany and Austria. At least 91 people died and 7,500 Jewish businesses were vandalized. More than 1,400 synagogues were targeted by arsonists, according to Israel’s Yad Vashem Holocaust memorial.
Shefi returned to the German capital 88 years later as one of the last living witnesses of Kristallnacht to share his memories at a time when antisemitism is on the rise again, not only in Germany but in many other countries around the globe.
Sitting on a bench in a nearby park where he was barred from sitting as a Jewish child, Shefi said he keeps those painful memories alive to help prevent such persecution from happening again.

item.title: Greek authorities find 12 bodies in a boat carrying migrants; 18 people are rescued
item.description:
Greek authorities find 12 bodies in a boat carrying migrants; 18 people are rescued
Greek authorities have recovered 12 bodies from a migrant boat found south of CreteByELENA BECATOROS Associated PressNovember 9, 2026, 1:02 AM
Share
ATHENS, Greece -- Greek authorities recovered 12 bodies from a boat carrying migrants found sailing south of Greece's island of Crete early Monday, while a passing Moroccan-flagged cargo ship rescued 18 people from the same vessel, the coast guard said.
No further information was immediately available on the identities of the 12 people who died, or the circumstances of their deaths. Greece’s coast guard said the boat they were traveling in was found about 15 nautical miles — about 28 kilometers or 18 miles — south of the southern Mediterranean island of Crete on Monday morning.
Another two boats, one carrying about 47 people and another with about 40 people on board, were also found sailing south of Crete. The first was spotted by an aircraft from the European Union's border agency Frontex, while the second was found by a Frontex drone, the coast guard said.
The agency added that those on board both boats were rescued by Frontex and were being taken to a port on the southern coast of Crete.
Greece is one of the main entry points into the European Union for people fleeing conflict and poverty in the Middle East, Africa and Asia. In recent months, thousands have been making the perilous sea crossing from north Africa, usually from Libya to Crete. Others make the far shorter but often equally dangerous crossing from the Turkish coast to nearby Greek islands in the Aegean Sea, often in unseaworthy inflatable dinghies or other small boats.

item.title: A pastor at a Beijing underground church has been arrested, his wife says
item.description:
A pastor at a Beijing underground church has been arrested, his wife says
Chinese authorities have arrested a pastor from a house church in Beijing, according to his wifeBySIMINA MISTREANU Associated Press and DIDI TANG Associated PressNovember 9, 2026, 12:40 AM
Share
TAIPEI, Taiwan -- A pastor of a house church in Beijing has been arrested, his wife told The Associated Press this week, as China intensifies its crackdown on unregistered churches.
Pastor Xianfeng Edward Cui, who founded Beijing Jiaquan Church, was arrested on Oct. 23 on charges of fraud, said his wife, Jin Young Gu, who lives outside of China.
Cui was first detained on Sept. 4 as part of a raid on his church that involved around 100 police officers, Gu said.
Gu said the fraud allegations are related to church members’ offerings. Such charges are likely related to the fact that the church is unregistered.
Police in Beijing’s Shijingshan district did not respond to a request for comment from The Associated Press. The Chinese Foreign Ministry did not answer questions about the pastor sent via a messaging app.
Cui's arrest is the latest case in Chinese President Xi Jinping's long-running campaign to tighten control over religion to ensure all groups of faith abide by Communist Party rule.
In one of the biggest crackdowns on religious activity in recent years, authorities in October 2025 arrested 30 leaders of Zion Church, one of the country’s largest underground church networks, following overnight raids in several cities.
Among those arrested was church founder Jin Mingri. He was freed in July following a personal request by U.S. President Donald Trump to Xi during Trump’s visit to Beijing.
Beijing Jiaquan Church was founded in 2006 and had grown in size as an unregistered congregation, Gu said.

item.title: Work to save the Afghan capital’s crumbling ancient fortress uncovers archaeological treasures
item.description:
Work to save the Afghan capital’s crumbling ancient fortress uncovers archaeological treasures
The imposing fortress of Bala Hissar in the Afghan capital Kabul has endured centuries of upheaval and warByELENA BECATOROS Associated PressNovember 9, 2026, 12:23 AM
KABUL, Afghanistan -- Perched high above the southern edge of Kabul’s old city, the imposing fortress of Bala Hissar has endured centuries of invasions, uprisings and conflict that scarred Afghanistan and left the citadel crumbling.
Now, an extensive, yearslong project by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture, or AKTC, is painstakingly conserving Bala Hissar. The aim is to turn the site into a public archaeological park, complete with landscaped gardens, restaurants and a museum.
Despite decades of neglect and war, archaeological treasures gradually unearthed within the walls of the strategic fortress in the Afghan capital are revealing more than two millennia of the country’s tumultuous history.
The excavations are uncovering an astonishing wealth of finds, from evidence of ancient human habitation to the remains of a Buddhist monastery and the luxurious baths of a Mughal palace.
“We never thought we would find so much,” said archaeologist Babak Rafiei-Alavi, standing at one of Bala Hissar’s excavation sites as workers with trowels painstakingly sifted through the earth. “It’s like a submarine coming out of the ocean.”
Work in five separate trenches at the site has unearthed ancient coins, fragments of Buddhist statues, glazed Islamic ceramics, oil lamps, countless pieces of pottery and the remains of palaces, monasteries and dwellings.
“In some parts we were expecting something. But not this,” Rafiei-Alavi said of the discovery of remnants of a Mughal palace, complete with murals, a thronelike structure and a star-shaped pool carved into the rock at the top of the hill.

item.title: Rubio will discuss Iran, Ukraine, AI and more with G7 allies in France
item.description:
Rubio will discuss Iran, Ukraine, AI and more with G7 allies in France
Secretary of State Marco Rubio will meet his counterparts from the Group of 7 industrialized democracies this weekByMATTHEW LEE AP diplomatic writerNovember 9, 2026, 12:01 AM
Share
PARIS -- U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will meet his counterparts from the Group of 7 industrialized democracies on Monday, with unresolved world crises on the agenda and questions about how President Donald Trump will approach foreign policy after his Republican Party’s massive losses in the midterm elections.
Two days of talks among the U.S., Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan in Paris coincide with major protests across Europe, including in the French capital.
The Russia-Ukraine war, the Iran conflict, energy and artificial intelligence are among the main topics for discussion. Many U.S. allies will be eager to hear how Trump plans to proceed on each.
The trip is Rubio's first foreign venture since the midterm elections dealt Trump's party severe losses and cost the GOP control of Congress, partly because of deeply unpopular policies like the Iran war.
Asked about allies wanting to know what comes next after the elections, Rubio told reporters that the countries he is meeting with this week understand American politics and “they, too, have experienced divisions in government and divisions in their own system.”
There has been little sign that the Democrats’ gains will affect Trump's strategy, and his first major personnel decision has installed a hard-line supporter, Stephen Miller, as chief of staff, who has advocated extreme positions on both domestic and foreign policy.
America's top diplomat is seen by many as presenting a gentler side to Trump’s often brusque approach to both friends and foes but there has been speculation — that he has denied — that he might choose to leave the administration early to prepare for a 2028 presidential run.

item.title: New Delhi wakes to toxic smog after Diwali firecrackers
item.description:
New Delhi wakes to toxic smog after Diwali firecrackers
A thick blanket of smog has shrouded India’s capital after firecrackers lit up the skies over New Delhi during Diwali celebrationsByRISHI LEKHI Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 10:07 PM
NEW DELHI -- A thick blanket of smog shrouded India’s capital Monday after firecrackers lit up the skies over New Delhi during Diwali celebrations, compounding dangerously high pollution levels and intensifying the seasonal air pollution crisis that grips the city every year.
Despite restrictions on fireworks, residents in New Delhi celebrated the Hindu festival of lights with firecrackers on Sunday evening, releasing smoke and fine particulate matter into the atmosphere. The air quality index exceeded 350 in several parts of the capital on Monday morning, reaching the severe category and posing significant health risks.
Monitoring stations across the city recorded similarly alarming levels, while visibility deteriorated as a gray haze blanketed streets and high-rise buildings.
India’s Supreme Court in October had sought to limit Diwali pollution by restricting conventional firecrackers and allowing only approved “green firecrackers” under specified conditions for three-hour windows on Saturday and Sunday. The crackers produce fewer emissions but are not pollution-free. They still release particulate matter and other pollutants, adding to the city’s already hazardous air.
Isyad, a New Delhi resident who uses one name, said the worsening smog was taking a toll on his health.
“Because of the pollution there is irritation in the throat and itching in the eyes,” he said.
New Delhi and its metropolitan region, home to more than 30 million people, regularly rank among the world’s most polluted areas during winter. Pollution worsens as Diwali fireworks coincide with cooler weather and smoke from crop-residue fires in neighboring states of Punjab and Haryana.

item.title: Leaders gather in Turkey for UN climate summit after a disastrous year of extreme weather
item.description:
Leaders gather in Turkey for UN climate summit after a disastrous year of extreme weather
World leaders, delegates and climate activists are gathering in Antalya, Turkey, for a U.N. climate summitBySUZAN FRASER Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 9:38 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
ANTALYA, Turkey -- World leaders, delegates and climate activists on Monday will begin negotiations on curbing climate change, which in the last year has led to rising temperatures, deadly heat waves in Europe and beyond, and has played a role in disasters like the devastating floods in Nepal.
This U.N. climate summit, called the Conference of the Parties, or COP31, also comes as the war in Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, pushing up global prices of gasoline and oil and myriad products made with them, such as fertilizers and pesticides. The disruption has pushed governments to rethink energy policies, both in the short-term and long-term, including increased investment in renewable energy sources like wind and solar.
Delegates, meeting in the Turkish Mediterranean resort city of Antalya, will come under pressure to develop new pledges for climate action while implementing previous promises. The stakes are high: climate scientists say global average temperature rise will exceed 1.5 C (2.7 F) since the early 1800s.
Limiting temperature rise to that threshold was a goal established during the 2015 Paris Agreement. Since then, it's been a focus of international climate negotiations. That the goal is no longer realistic underscores how difficult it's been for the world to cut greenhouse gas emissions, which are released into the atmosphere when fossil fuels like oil, gas and coal are burned, leading to climate change.
“This is the first COP where it is clear beyond a reasonable doubt that the world will overshoot the 1.5-degree target,” said Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum. “We will not look away, and we will not lower our ambition.”

item.title: Kidnapped Mexican border town mayor found alive
item.description:
Kidnapped Mexican border town mayor found alive
He was kidnapped for several hours while traveling in the state of Zacatecas.ByALFREDO PEÑA Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 4:09 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
CIUDAD VICTORIA, Mexico -- The mayor of a Mexican border town was found alive Sunday after he was kidnapped for several hours while traveling in the northern state of Zacatecas, federal officials said.
Miguel Angel Almaraz was traveling with family and friends Saturday in a region that straddles the states of Zacatecas and San Luis de Potosi, when his car was intercepted by armed men, who took Almaraz and let his family go.
According to the Security Department of San Luis Potosi, Almaraz’s relatives were able to reach a town in that state, where they alerted authorities about the kidnapping.
Officials said that Almaraz was taken to the city of Zacatecas, where he was released by his captors. The case is under investigation.

Almaraz is the mayor of Rio Bravo, a municipality of about 110,000 people in Tamaulipas state. The city is located just seven miles (11 kilometers) from Mexico's border with Texas.
